methodological_rigor.justification: The design uses a reasonable multi-cohort structure (TCGA training N=234; three external validation cohorts GSE30219 N=78, GSE31210 N=168, FUSCC N=70) and benchmarks 10 ML algorithms plus combinations, selecting StepCox[forward]+Ridge by C-index. Multivariable Cox analyses support MAPI as an independent predictor across cohorts, strengthening internal validity. However, no sample-size justification or power calculation is reported, the authors themselves acknowledge that nested cross-validation / hyperparameter tuning was not performed (risking optimism bias from model selection on validation C-indices), and the scRNA-seq validation is based on only 9 patients. Multiplicity correction across the many pathway, immune, and drug-sensitivity comparisons is not described, and the in vitro functional work is confined to two cell lines (A549, H358) with n=3-5 replicates and no mention of blinded scoring or independent biological replicates. Reliance on retrospective public data with in silico drug-sensitivity inference further limits causal inference.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective, multi-cohort prognostic biomarker development and validation study with ancillary preclinical functional work, best classified as Oxford 2b (individual cohort study with external validation; the molecular/functional components fall at level 5 but do not drive the main clinical claim). Clinically, the question is important — stage I LUAD has heterogeneous outcomes and TNM alone poorly identifies candidates for adjuvant therapy — and endpoints are patient-relevant (DFS, OS). However, drug-response predictions (paclitaxel, bortezomib, vincristine) and immunotherapy predictions are entirely in silico (GDSC/CTRP/CMap, TIDE, IPS, SubMap vs. a melanoma ACT cohort), making translational claims hypothesis-generating only. Without prospective validation or a biomarker-directed interventional study, the index is not practice-changing.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the applicable standard because the study develops and externally validates a multivariable prognostic model. The paper reports cohort sources, inclusion/exclusion (follow-up <3 months excluded), candidate predictors (548 core metabolic genes), the modeling strategy, discrimination (C-index, time-dependent AUCs), and independent predictor status via multivariable Cox — covering many TRIPOD items. Key gaps include no model calibration (calibration plots, Brier scores), no clear handling of missing data, no decision-curve analysis, no reporting of model equation/coefficients in the main text, no protocol pre-registration, and incomplete reporting of the in vitro methods (shRNA sequences, antibodies, statistical tests) in the main text. All underlying omics datasets are public and clearly identified (TCGA; GSE30219, GSE31210, GSE100797, GSE189357; EGAS00001004006), supporting replicability, but no custom analysis code repository (e.g., GitHub/Zenodo) is cited.

novelty_literature.justification: The conceptual novelty is modest: metabolism-based prognostic signatures in LUAD, including stage-I-focused ones, have been published previously (the authors cite refs 10 and 11 explicitly as metabolic/lipid-metabolism signatures in early-stage LUAD), and the WGCNA + ML-combination pipeline (Mime1) applied here is a well-trodden recipe in TCGA prognostic-signature papers. Empirical novelty lies in the specific gene composition of MAPI and the dual focus on stage I only, plus functional confirmation that DEGS1 and PLOD1 knockdown suppresses LUAD proliferation and migration — but PLOD1 oncogenic roles across cancers (including the mechanisms cited by the authors) and DEGS1 effects on cell cycle/apoptosis are already established. Methodological novelty is limited, and the in silico drug repositioning claims (paclitaxel, bortezomib, vincristine) overlap with earlier CMap/GDSC analyses in NSCLC. Overall, this is incremental extension of known approaches rather than a conceptual advance.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with a logical IMRaD flow; the abstract is self-contained and accurately mirrors the results; and figure captions describe panels in enough detail to be interpretable without seeing the figures. Terminology (WGCNA, OCLR, mRNAsi, TIDE, IPS, SubMap, CytoTRACE, CMap) is introduced with sufficient context, and limitations are explicitly enumerated in the Discussion. Minor issues include some awkward phrasing ('immunologically activate'), occasionally dense sentences linking multiple findings, and a Discussion that leans heavily on narrative pathway speculation (e.g., sphingomyelin/water 'hydrogen barrier') not directly tested. Overall presentation is publication-quality with light copyediting needed.

key_strengths: Multi-cohort external validation (TCGA + GSE30219 + GSE31210 + FUSCC) with consistent DFS/OS stratification and independent prognostic value on multivariable Cox
Comprehensive benchmarking of 10 ML algorithms and combinations with transparent C-index selection
Integration of bulk, single-cell (GSE189357), genomic (TMB, mutational landscape), and immune (TIDE/IPS/SubMap) layers with in vitro DEGS1/PLOD1 knockdown validation in two LUAD cell lines
Clear writing, informative figure captions, and explicit acknowledgment of key limitations including the absence of nested cross-validation
All underlying omics datasets are public and identifiable, enabling reproducibility of the modeling pipeline
key_concerns: Incremental novelty: metabolism-based LUAD prognostic signatures and the WGCNA+Mime1 ML-combination recipe are well established (authors cite refs 10, 11 as direct comparators)
No calibration metrics, decision-curve analysis, missing-data handling, or model-equation/coefficients disclosure — key TRIPOD items for a prediction model are missing
No power/sample-size justification; no nested CV (authors acknowledge); risk of optimism bias from selecting the final model by validation-cohort C-index

Drug repositioning (paclitaxel, bortezomib, vincristine) and immunotherapy-response claims are entirely in silico, and the SubMap comparison uses a melanoma ACT cohort as the only immunotherapy anchor
In vitro validation limited to two cell lines, n=3-5, with no blinding, no shRNA sequence details, and no in vivo confirmation
No analysis-code repository is cited despite reliance on multiple R pipelines
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competently executed but incremental multi-omics prognostic-signature paper for stage I LUAD with external validation and limited functional confirmation; the mix of modest novelty, missing TRIPOD items (calibration, model disclosure), and purely in silico therapeutic claims places its ceiling at tier 3 journals (e.g., BMC Cancer / European J Cancer level) and warrants major revisions to add calibration, release the model, and temper translational claims.
